title: Busy-path tests take the lock wait as a per-call input

epic.name: Async test suite through dependency injection

story.i_want_to: give the call I am testing a short lock wait
story.so_that: I stop waiting out the deployed 5s while the race tests keep their full margin

rationale: The slowest sync modules wait out Loopctl.Runners.Capacity's 5s lock_timeout once per busy-path test. Measured on minis, 2026-10-07: the six slowest delivery modules took 168.6 s at 5s and 101.6 s with the wait at 2s (402 tests, 0 failures), and the gate's test step fell from about 254 s to 165 s at 1s. A suite-wide test-config value was tried in PR #954 and withdrawn after two review rounds: the race tests (up to ten callers on one lock, exact outcome counts) need the full wait, the busy-path tests want a short one, and one knob cannot serve both. Production sets lock_timeout inside its own transaction, so a test cannot shorten it from outside.

acceptance_criteria.description: The Capacity entry points the busy-path tests exercise take the lock wait as an option defaulting to Capacity.lock_timeout_ms/0 (5s); production callers pass nothing and behave exactly as today.
The option is never fed from request data or channel params; it carries no identity (CLAUDE.md, custody identity).
The busy-path tests in VerificationRunnerWorkerIntegration, RunnerChannelDispatch, MergePreconditionIntegration and Capacity pass a short wait; the race tests pass nothing.
The PR reports the six slow modules' time and the gate's test step before and after.

test_cases.name: Busy path answers within the injected wait
steps: Hold the runner row on a second connection
Call the entry point with a 100ms wait

test_cases.name: Seam is load-bearing
steps: Make the entry point ignore the option
expected_results: The test fails on elapsed time

technical_notes: Capacity.set_lock_timeout!/1 is the one place the wait is applied; thread an optional ms through it from the entry points the busy tests call.
Channel-process paths (RunnerChannelDispatch) need the wait to reach the channel; a socket-assign set only by test setup, never from connect params, is one route.
